children: Beena Parmar Bengaluru: US-based IT services major Cognizant has signed a new large deal worth over $100 million with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) for five years. While the firms did not disclose the financial details, the deal is estimated to be worth $100-150 million, with annual revenue of around $26-40 million, two people told ET. "The deal is a new one and likely in the range of £20-30 million (approximately $26-40 million) a year," a person privy to the development told ET. According to Phil Fersht, founder and chief analyst of US-based technology consultancy HFS Research, "The potential five-year value is around $100 million, with a plausible range of $75 million-$125 million.

That is a scope-and-spend-based estimate, not a disclosed figure, and the framework structure means actual revenue will depend on the work commissioned." Cognizant and EBRD did not immediately respond to ET's request for comment on the deal size and scope of work. Large IT deals for major software services providers are typically worth over $100 million.

Over the past two years, such deals have come under pressure due to a slowdown in business and have been further affected by disruption following the advent of AI. Such deals have shifted towards AI-driven digital transformation, vendor consolidation and efficiency improvement projects. Moreover, converting deals into revenue has been a major challenge for most firms.

Over the past three weeks, India's top five IT majors reported nearly $20 billion in deal bookings, less than the $22 billion reported by Ireland-based Accenture, the world's largest IT services firm. Infosys, the second-largest IT firm, reported the highest deal wins, at $5.2 billion, including one worth over $2 billion.

Cognizant, which has over 70% of its employees in India, will report its earnings on October 29. The US-headquartered company's deal with EBRD will support the bank's technology transformation programme, driving innovation through digitally enabled processes involving AI, data and automation, Cognizant said in a statement.

Under the five-year framework, Cognizant aims to deliver critical technology services through two complementary models: outcome-led managed services and fixed-capacity services. These will span digital and workplace management, cloud infrastructure, data and security, software engineering, automation and AI. The framework also includes a programme of continuous improvement and innovation designed to enhance services, strengthen resilience and deliver measurable value over time, it added. "As an AI Builder, Cognizant's role is to help clients turn their technology investments into dependable operations and measurable outcomes, and that only happens when services are made to work across the complexity of a real enterprise estate," said Rohit Gupta, managing director for the UK and Ireland at Cognizant. "The EBRD operates in a demanding, highly governed environment across three continents. By combining our decades of industry experience, end-to-end systems integration expertise, and AI-enabled operational capabilities within a collaborative framework, we will help the EBRD run its critical technology services with confidence and accelerate the modernisation and innovation that drive its mission," Gupta added.

title: Cognizant Bags Five-Year EBRD Deal Worth Up to $150 Million
